pages.title: The Admission
pages.text: They put me out of my homeland, and I answered by leaving the world. Then I needed its water. Its wheat. Its coal.$(br2)So I ran lines back to it. I tell myself that a pipe is not a visit.
$(item)Item conduits$(): roots of obsidian with light crawling in them. They join each other and whatever holds things. Eight at a time.
$(item)Fluid conduits$(), the same with lapis. Water was the first thing I sent through. I stood and watched it arrive, like a fool.
$(item)Energy conduits$(), with gold. The three kinds never join one another: a line carries one sort of thing.
The $(item)rift tuner$(). An end $(thing)pushes$() at first. One use makes it $(thing)pull$(), the next $(thing)seals$() it, the next opens it again. Nothing moves until an end pulls.

pages.title: How Much
pages.text: A pulling end takes sixteen items, a bucket of fluid or 4,000 of energy every half second, and hands it to each pushing end in turn.$(br2)From a furnace it takes what is finished. Into one, it puts fuel and ore each where it belongs.
